properties.name: Pro Juventute 'Hilfswerk für die Kinder der Landstrasse'
properties.group: Swiss Yenish children
properties.what: Pro Juventute's programme, started by Alfred Siegfried, took about 586–600 Yenish children from their families and placed them in foster homes, children's homes, psychiatric clinics and prisons. On 20 February 2025 the Federal Council recognised the persecution of Yenish and Sinti travellers as a crime against humanity. Figures: 586 Yenish children 1926–1973 (Swissinfo); about 2,000 Traveller children taken in total; later compensation total 11 million francs, max 20,000 per person

properties.name: UK Child Migrant Programme (UK apology 2010)
properties.group: British child migrants
properties.what: More than 130,000 children aged 3 to 14 were sent from the UK to Commonwealth countries including Canada, Australia, South Africa and Rhodesia between the 1920s and 1960s. Prime Minister Gordon Brown apologised in the House of Commons on 24 February 2010 and announced a £6 million family restoration fund. Figures: More than 130,000 children; £6 million fund

Later Keaney College, it closed at the end of 2024.

properties.name: Longhui county family-planning officials seized babies for orphanage adoption
properties.group: Babies seized for orphanage adoption (China)
properties.placed at: Longhui County, Hunan (the middle of the region named)
properties.what: Caixin reported in May 2011 that family-planning officials in Longhui county near Shaoyang seized at least 16 babies from families unable to pay fines for breaching birth limits and passed them to welfare centres that listed them for adoption, including overseas; one migrant worker reportedly found her daughter had been adopted in the United States. The Shaoyang government opened an investigation. Figures: At least 16 babies; family-planning office reportedly received 1,000 yuan or more per child; welfare centres up to $3,000 (or $3,000–5,000) per overseas adoption
